title: Foreign Workers (Prohibition of Unlawful Employment and Assurance of Fair Conditions) Law, 5751-1991
amended: amended several times (consolidated English text undated)
source_tier: Secondary (UNHCR Refworld; unofficial English translation of a consolidated version)
site_status: NEW: add to national-laws (already cited in the domestic-workers database as Foreign Workers Law, 1991)
note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the Refworld PDF supplied by IMR (unofficial English, consolidated with later amendments, date of consolidation not stated). Known as the Foreign Workers Law. In force 1 May 1991. Employer may employ a foreign worker only with a medical certificate, a written contract in a language the worker understands (s. 1C), medical insurance (s. 1D) and suitable housing (s. 1E); deposits into a Foreign Workers Fund paid to the worker on departure (Chapter Four, s. 1K), with exemptions or reductions possible for nursing-care (caregiver) workers employed by individuals; offences and supervision in Chapter Five. Same PDF also on ecoi.net (ACCORD): https://www.ecoi.net/en/file/local/1070205/1226_1279194761_4c36ed992.pdf. Official Hebrew text to find on Nevo or the Knesset legislation database.

title: Employment of Employees by Manpower Contractors (Application for Licence) Regulations, 5756-1996
title_original: תקנות העסקת עובדים על ידי קבלני כוח אדם (בקשה לרשיון), תשנ"ו-1996
source_tier: Secondary (israelilegislation.com, private site; unofficial English translation of the consolidated Hebrew text as of 2023-09-18)
note: Read on 2026-11-21 in the built-in browser. Only the Hebrew text in Reshumot is binding; official Hebrew text still to find (Nevo or the Knesset database). Made under ss. 2(d) and 25 of the Employment of Employees by Manpower Contractors Law, 5756-1996 (the parent Law is not yet in our tables). Licence applications to the Minister of Labour with an affidavit, office conditions (incl. a private interview room for job candidates) and the data needed to set the guarantee amount; consent to criminal-record checks of managers; decision within three months (reg. 4). The Foreign Workers Law, 5751-1991 adopts this Law's definition of 'manpower contractor'.

title: Prevention of Infiltration Law (Offenses and Jurisdiction), 5714-1954
amended: Amendment No. 3 and Temporary Order 5772-2012; Legislative Amendments and Temporary Order 2014 (and later amendments to Aug 2018)
source_tier: Secondary (UNHCR Israel; unofficial English translation, consolidated version as of August 2018)
note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the unofficial consolidated English translation (Aug 2018) published by UNHCR Israel (link from IMR). Official Hebrew text to find on Nevo or the Knesset database. Defines an 'infiltrator' as a non-resident who entered other than through a designated border crossing (s. 1); offences ss. 2-9; presumption that anyone who entered without permission or stays unlawfully is an infiltrator (s. 10); deportation orders by the Minister of Defense (s. 30); custody, review by the Director of Border Control and release on guarantee (ss. 30A-30D); detention conditions (s. 30B); residence orders and Residency Centers (ss. 32A-32D, the 'Holot' facility). The Supreme Court struck down earlier detention provisions in Adam v. Knesset (2013), already in our decisions table (il-adam-2013).

note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the Argus English translation supplied by IMR (text as at early 2010). Art. 7 excludes domestic servants employed in private houses and agricultural enterprises not connected with trade or industry (the latter left to a special law). Art. 12: written contract in Arabic, may be translated for a foreign worker. Art. 59: foreign workers get Lebanese workers' rights on dismissal only on condition of reciprocity and must hold a work permit. title: Law of 10 July 1962 Regulating the Entry and Stay of Foreigners in Lebanon and their Exit
topic: entry; residence; removal; work permits; asylum
in_force: day after publication in the Official Gazette (art. 40)
source_tier: Secondary (L'Argus English translation, hosted on ILO NATLEX, record 39234)
site_status: NEW: add to national-laws; parent law of Order No. 319 of 1962 already on the site
note: Checked on 2026-11-21 against the NATLEX PDF supplied by IMR (Argus translation; all rights reserved). Signed at Zouk on 10 July 1962 (President Fouad Chehab; Interior Minister Kamal Joumblatt). Art. 6: entry only through General Security posts; a foreigner coming to work needs a prior permit from the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (artists from General Security). Art. 12: one-year and three-year residence cards. Art. 17-18: expulsion by the Director of General Security, with detention pending removal on the Public Prosecutor's approval. Art. 19: travel pass for stateless persons and refugees. Art. 25: no work without a Ministry of Labour permit. Arts. 26-31: political asylum, with a ban on expelling a former political refugee to a country where life or freedom is threatened (art. 31). Arts. 32-36: penalties, incl. imprisonment and expulsion for irregular entry. Official Arabic text still to find.

title: Instructions No. 1 of 2026 on Recruiting, Employing and Licensing Foreign Workers in Iraq
topic: labor; work permits; recruitment; domestic workers
site_status: LEAD: official text needed before publishing
note: Described in a Baghdad law firm's article of 10 Oct 2026 (not read in the original). Issued under art. 33 of Labour Law No. 37 of 2015; replaces the 1987 instructions; federal Iraq only (Kurdistan Region has its own procedures). Reported content: permit from the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs before any work; labour market test against the ministry's job-seeker database; foreign workers capped at 50% of a project's workforce; domestic workers capped at two per household unless approved; one-year renewable permit; contract in Arabic and English or the worker's mother tongue (art. 9); employer must report an absconding worker to the ministry and police (art. 8); eight cancellation grounds (art. 10). Find the Arabic text in Al-Waqa'i al-Iraqiyya No. 4863 (Ministry of Justice) before use.
